title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation per intent, reused for both episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. Important scope note: the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the confirmatory estimand and the numerical inference reported here apply only to the executed synthetic/emulation partition. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as intent-to-configuration translators for network operations (NetOps): given an operator intent in natural language, produce device CLI sequences that enact the intent. The stochastic nature of modern LLMs yields operational risk classes relevant to NetOps: syntactic errors, incorrect command ordering, workflow-violation sequences (e.g., breaking make-before-break invariants), and vendor-CLI subtleties that can create service disruption. A recurring architectural mitigation is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that interposes a deterministic validator between LLM generation and acceptance, optionally permitting bounded automated repair attempts when the validator fails. Prior surveys and empirical reports document LLM feasibility for producing draft configurations under constrained conditions while noting remaining verification needs [1],[2].

This paper empirically isolates the marginal verifier-and-single-repair effect under the strictly defined shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one initial model generation is produced per intent and that identical candidate is reused across the paired comparison (baseline = accept candidate; guarded = validate and, if failing, permit one automated repair). This design measures only downstream validator-and-repair marginal effects on identical generated outputs rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. The experiment was preregistered, executed, and fully archived; the principal contribution is an artifact-grounded numeric bound on the verifier-detected improvement for a constrained NetOps task set when using a single repair attempt.
sections.related_work:
Work on LLMs for NetOps has rapidly expanded: multiple surveys and task-specific studies report that LLMs can construct syntactically plausible and operationally useful configuration drafts in emulation or constrained testbeds [1],[2],[3]. Deterministic network verifiers and formal-analysis tools (e.g., Batfish-style analyses, header-space/model-based approaches, and incremental verification methods) are established techniques used to check forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties; these are commonly adopted as validators in GVR pipelines [4],[5]. In adjacent domains, generate-and-verify and program-repair architectures have improved detection and correction of mechanically verifiable defects in code-generation and configuration tasks, though semantic correctness beyond mechanically checkable properties remains challenging [6]. Security analyses emphasize prompt-injection and retrieval-sourced threats to LLM-integrated applications and motivate layered defenses that include validation and filtering [7].

Our work differs along three axes: (i) the preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates validator/repair marginal effects on identical candidates, (ii) deterministic reconciliation of provider-call accounting to demonstrate stage-level mapping (shared generation vs repair), and (iii) archival publication of validator traces and analysis artifacts so reported numeric outcomes are auditable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 with a confirmatory paired design (N_pairs = 250), generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy (one automated repair allowed per episode), exclusion/contamination rules, and the analysis plan (exact McNemar two-sided test plus paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI). The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the evidence bundle and cited in the Disclosure Statement.

Task bank and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break, simultaneous-MTU constraints, protected interfaces). Tasks were labeled by difficulty (medium/hard/very_hard) and designed to exercise ordering and group-activity constraints representative of operational change workflows.

Model and invocation policy. The declared model for all initial generations was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Per shared_initial_candidate semantics, the pipeline executed exactly one shared initial generation call per intent and reused the same generated candidate for both baseline and guarded episodes; independent first-pass generation per condition was not performed. The preregistered adapter allowed up to one automated repair call per episode; execution used this policy but exercised only one repair in the run. Provider-call accounting reconciles to hosted_model_call_event_count = 251, mapping to 250 shared initial-generation events and 1 repair-stage call.

Validator and repair design. The guarded pipeline applied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation: syntactic parsing of CLI sequences, matching parsed_command_count to required_command_count, enforcing required_sequence and workflow constraints (group-activity and make-before-break rules), computing a final_state snapshot, and comparing it to the task-encoded expected_final_state. Validator outputs included normalized_configuration and a boolean valid flag. When valid = false the pipeline permitted a single automated repair attempt applying deterministic, template-constrained fixes (reordering commands to match required_sequence, splitting/normalizing multi-command lines, correcting obvious command-token ordering). Repaired candidates were re-submitted to the validator; no further iterations or human escalation were permitted in the confirmatory run.

Inclusion, contamination, and handling of technical failures. The preregistration excluded episodes where vendor-parser failure prevented deterministic verification, or where denylist/credential-like tokens were detected. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged items were to be excluded from the primary analysis and treated in sensitivity analyses. The missingness policy allowed one immediate retry on LLM API error; unrecoverable provider/API failures were handled per the preregistered rules and logged. In this run no episodes were excluded or flagged for contamination.
sections.results:
Execution summary and reconciliation. Execution completed planned_episode_count = 500 (250 pairs × 2 episodes), completed_episode_count = 500, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 251. Provider-call accounting recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}, consistent with the shared_initial_candidate semantics and a single exercised repair. Complete_pair_count = 250; no episodes were excluded or unscorable.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Deterministic validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Observed paired contingency: n11 = 249 (passed both), n10 = 1 (failed baseline, passed guarded), n01 = 0 (passed baseline, failed guarded), n00 = 0 (failed both). The single discordant pair corresponds to the sole exercised repair; repair-conversion rate in the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%). The contingency counts are recorded in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.

Statistical inference. We applied the preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test to the discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0), yielding p = 1.0. We computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729); the CI is [0.0, 0.012] expressed in absolute proportion (i.e., 0–1.2 percentage points). These numeric results and the bootstrap parameters are archived in the analysis log.

Representative validator diagnostics. Passed episodes show parsed_command_count matching the task's required_command_count. Example: task-000003 (hard difficulty) had parsed_command_count = 6, required_command_count = 6, valid = true in both baseline and guarded episodes. Representative raw responses and normalized configurations for example tasks are archived in execution/responses and execution/scoring artifacts.

Repair exercise. Only one automated repair call occurred; that repair converted the sole failing baseline candidate into a guarded-pass. No other repairs were triggered for the confirmatory partition.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the near‑null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the sole failing candidate was corrected by the permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) bounds the maximum verifier-detected improvement on this task set under the implemented pipeline.

Artifact-grounded reasons for the small observed gain. Three archival, run-grounded factors explain the limited observed improvement: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents, allowed_touched_fields, and required_sequences that reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI outputs; (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced highly consistent and syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator measured mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshots) and therefore cannot detect broader live-protocol or emergent behavioral correctness absent in the task encoding.

Power, assumptions, and consequence. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to detect a 15 percentage-point absolute effect at ≈80% power. The observed baseline pass rate (0.996) was substantially higher than assumed, reducing our ability to detect small absolute improvements; thus the paired-bootstrap CI is the more informative practical bound for this study. The exact McNemar p-value and the small number of discordant pairs underscore the constrained evidence: a rare failing candidate was corrected by a single automated repair, but larger or adversarial task banks could yield qualitatively different outcomes.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: outcomes depend on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, the shared_initial_candidate design, and the precise validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator assesses mechanically checkable correctness but does not assert live protocol-level correctness or performance effects. External validity: the confirmatory evidence applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition executed here; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed in this run. Security and robustness: adaptive prompt-injection, retrieval-based contamination, and adversarial vectors were not exercised and remain open threats. Multi-model generality is not established because only the declared gpt-5-mini model was used.

Operational implication (bounded). In tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM, the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single, deterministic repair may be small. This finding does not imply validators or repairs are unnecessary in broader operational settings: wider validator scope, multi-iteration repair policies, human escalation pathways, production heterogeneity, and adversarial inputs can materially change the benefit calculus.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. On N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks the initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed; the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived and available in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human and autonomy roles: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and execution accounting (concise): declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode. Confirmatory execution completed planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation calls + 1 repair) with stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}, consistent with preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics. These numeric reconciliation facts are reported in the paper and archived in the evidence bundle.

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the evidence bundle). Immutable master prompt initiating the autonomous run is archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Archival pointer and scope note: the full execution and analysis artifact bundle (raw model responses, execution manifests, validator traces, repair traces, provider-call audit, and analysis CSVs) is archived and referenced in the evidence bundle associated with this submission; readers and auditors should consult that bundle for per-artifact verification. Important deviation disclosure: the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the reported confirmatory estimand and numerical inference apply only to the executed synthetic/emulation partition (N_pairs = 250) under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshots) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.

Realized baseline pass-rate (0.996) substantially exceeded the preregistered power-assumption (~0.90), reducing the study's power to detect small absolute improvements; consequently, the paired-bootstrap CI is the most informative practical bound from this run.
